newsitem.title: INDIA: DSP Merrill Lynch sees investment surge in India.
newsitem.headline: DSP Merrill Lynch sees investment surge in India.

text.p: DSP Merrill Lynch Asset Management (India) Ltd said on Wednesday that it expects the Indian government's proposed budget to trigger a heavy inflow of foreign direct investment into the country.
"The foreign direct investments are expected to improve dramatically," the company said at a news conference ahead of the launch of two open-ended mutual funds in New Delhi.
The DSP Merrill Lynch Bond Fund and the DSP Merrill Lynch Equity Fund will be open for subscription from April 7 through April 15.
The company predicted bold tax cuts introduced in the budget for 197/98 (April-March) would spur economic growth.
Foreign institutional investors made net purchases of $101.1 million between March 1 and 12 after the budget was unveiled on February 28.
The budget proposed cutting taxes and raising foreign portfolio limits in firms to 30 percent from 24 percent.
Inflows in February totalled $88.8 million and in January they were $89.3 million, according to the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
"The entry of new players both domestic and foreign will contribute to greater liquidity and depth in the Indian capital markets," DSP Merrill Lynch said.
DSP Merrill Lynch Asset Management is a venture of investment bank DSP Merrill Lynch and Merrill Lynch Asset Management. DSP Merrill Lynch is the Indian affiliate of the U.S. investment bank.
